title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.72-74, 10 July 1986): Grothendieck sets up an abstract theory of 'disjonctions', which leads on the next page to 'syntaxes'. A disjunction on a set E is a relation x|o|y satisfying two axioms. Disj 1: the relation is symmetric. Disj 2: if x|o|x then x|o|y for every y. E_0 is the set of self-disjoint points; such points are disjoint from everything. The antireflexive case is E_0 = ∅. On the previous page he identifies antireflexive disjunctions with simple graphs (the edges are the disjoint pairs).

The operator. For A ⊂ E, the operator he writes cos-W°_E or cosimpl°_E is, in modern terms, the Galois polarity A^⊥ = {y : y|o|a for all a ∈ A}. The closure he writes W°_E or simpl°_E is A^⊥⊥. Σ_E ⊂ P(E) is the family of closed parts.
- Σ_E is stable under arbitrary intersections.
- Its top element is E and its bottom element is E_0. Indeed ∅^⊥⊥ = E^⊥ = E_0, using Disj 2.
- Σ_E is therefore a complete lattice: Inf is ∩, while Sup is in general not ∪.
- C S := S^⊥ is an order-reversing involution on Σ_E.
- The map σ: E → Σ_E, x ↦ {x}^⊥⊥, sends points to the 'atoms' of Σ_E.

Trivial disjunction. If x|o|y ⇔ x ≠ y, then E_0 = ∅ and A^⊥ = E∖A, so Σ_E = P(E).

NB (reduction step). E_0 is contained in every A^⊥ and every A^⊥⊥, and both depend only on A ∪ E_0, equivalently on A* = A∖(E_0∩A). Hence S ↦ S∖E_0 and S* ↦ S* ⊔ E_0 give an isomorphism Σ_E ≅ Σ_{E*}, with E* = E∖E_0. This isomorphism is compatible with the order and with C. So one reduces to the antireflexive case, where Σ is a complete ortholattice. That is exactly what p.74 axiomatizes as a 'syntaxe' (Synt 1-3): a complete lattice with an order-reversing involution C such that x∧Cx = 0.

Rotated margin note. It apparently characterizes σ by x|o|y ⇔ σx ⊥ σy, i.e. σx ⊂ Cσy, and defines A|o|B for subsets A, B via cos-W°(A) ⊃ B, etc.

In modern terms: orthogonality spaces (orthogonality spaces / orthoframes), and the complete ortholattice of their biorthogonally closed subsets. The degenerate points E_0 are split off.
errors: For the trivial disjunction x|o|y ⇔ x≠y, the graph of disjoint pairs defined on the previous page is the COMPLETE graph, not 'A=∅, structure de graphe discrète'. The statement is consistent only if the graph is taken to be the complement (compatibility) graph, so there is a convention slip.
Minor: the rotated margin note is fragmentary, and the claimed characterization of σ is not fully written out.
The fact that Sup in Σ_E is not ∪ is stated correctly. Orthomodularity is not claimed, which is correct: Σ_E is in general only an ortholattice.

ideas.what: A symmetric 'disjunction' relation, with degenerate self-disjoint points E_0 that are disjoint from everything
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space / orthoframe (irreflexive symmetric relation), plus null points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall; Goldblatt (1974, orthoframes); also MacLaren (1964)

ideas.what: Closed parts under the biorthogonal closure A ↦ A^⊥⊥ form a complete lattice with order-reversing involution, with E_0 as bottom
Reduction Σ_E ≅ Σ_{E∖E_0} by removing the degenerate points
Trivial disjunction x≠y gives the Boolean algebra P(E); antireflexive disjunctions correspond to simple graphs
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality graphs; the discrete case gives a Boolean lattice

missed.claim: Historical: in July 1986 Grothendieck independently re-develops the theory of orthogonality spaces and complete ortholattices, which he calls 'disjonctions' and 'syntaxes'. This is apparently a foundational/logical formalization, and it is not documented in accounts of his post-1984 work. The mathematics itself is standard (quantum-logic literature, 1960s-70s).
missed.quote: parties Σ_E de P_E, stables par ∩ quelconques, ayant comme plus grand élément E, comme plus petit élément E_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an otherwise unknown strand of his late work (lattice/ortho-logic foundations). There is no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a clean but standard rediscovery of orthogonality spaces and their complete ortholattices of closed sets. It is interesting only biographically.
transcription_corrections: 'compatible aux structures d'ordre et ∩' should read 'compatible aux structures d'ordre et C' (complementation).
'la cellule simplexe E_0' is likely just 'comme plus petit élément E_0'.
'C S =df cosimpl°_E A' should be read as C S = cos-W°_E S (the polar of S), with S ∈ Σ_E ⊂ P(E).
'A* = A ∖ E_0 ∩ A' means A* = A ∖ (E_0 ∩ A).
The isomorphism line reads S ↦ S∖E_0 and S* ⊔ E_0 ← S*.
